clinician.trajectory_summary: A previously healthy 2-year-old Emirati boy with incomplete immunizations (stopped at 4 months) presented to the emergency department with septic shock (hypotension 80/50 mmHg, tachycardia 137 bpm, capillary refill 4 seconds) and altered mental status (GCS 10-11) following a week of URI symptoms and presumed viral gastroenteritis. CSF analysis revealed purulent meningitis (WBC 5566/μL with 89% polys, protein 105 mg/dL, glucose 35 mg/dL, ratio 0.4) with Gram-negative coccobacilli on stain. CSF and blood cultures confirmed BLNAR Haemophilus influenzae type b. Empiric therapy with intravenous ceftriaxone (200 mg/kg/day) and dexamethasone was initiated. CT head showed mild diffuse cerebral edema without raised intracranial pressure. On day 7, persistent fever prompted repeat blood cultures revealing ceftriaxone resistance; therapy was changed to meropenem (120 mg/kg/day) with prompt defervescence. MRI on day 8 demonstrated subdural empyema requiring neurosurgical consultation. Follow-up MRI on day 16 confirmed resolution of subdural pus pockets prior to discharge.

Follow-up MRI on day 16 prior to discharge confirmed resolution of subdural pus pockets

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Initially diagnosed elsewhere but ruled out by presence of septic shock, altered mental status, and CSF findings confirming bacterial meningitis (E002, E006)
Specific identification of Haemophilus influenzae type b by culture excluded Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and other bacterial causes (E014)
CSF neutrophilic pleocytosis (89% polys), markedly elevated protein, and low glucose ratio are inconsistent with viral etiology (E006)

remaining_uncertainties: Exact total duration of antibiotic therapy from admission to discharge
Specific neurological examination findings at discharge
Whether subdural empyema required surgical drainage or resolved with antibiotic therapy alone (neurosurgical opinion sought but no procedure documented)

evaluation.known_final_diagnosis: CSF and blood cultures confirmed beta-lactamase-negative ampicillin-resistant (BLNAR) Haemophilus influenzae type b meningitis susceptible to ceftriaxone, meropenem, and cefotaxime
